q: An attacker enters a local network address into a website form, causing the web server to send an unauthorized HTTP request to an internal system behind the firewall. What attack occurred?
opts: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
Structured query injection (SQLi)
Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
exp: SSRF occurs when an attacker tricks a backend server into initiating unauthorized network requests to internal or loopback resources.

wrongFeedback.0: XSS executes malicious scripts inside a victim’s client browser rather than forcing a backend server to query internal networks.
wrongFeedback.1: SQLi injects malicious syntax into database queries to manipulate data, not sending outbound network requests.
wrongFeedback.3: CSRF tricks an authenticated client browser into submitting unwanted actions to a website, rather than the server making requests.

q: Which mitigation directly prevents server-side request forgery (SSRF) by restricting the external web addresses an application server is allowed to fetch?
opts: Enforcing a strict destination URL allowlist
Configuring HttpOnly flags on session cookies
Implementing parameterized SQL database queries
Enforcing complex multi-factor authentication
exp: URL allowlisting explicitly limits the domains and IP addresses the server can query, blocking calls to loopback or private internal addresses.

wrongFeedback.1: The `HttpOnly` flag stops client-side scripts from reading session cookies during XSS attacks, but does not limit server network calls.
wrongFeedback.2: Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection at the database tier, providing no control over server-initiated HTTP requests.
wrongFeedback.3: MFA verifies human user identity during authentication, but does not stop an application from fetching unauthorized external URLs.

q: An attacker submits http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/ into an invoice import field on a cloud-hosted app, successfully exfiltrating temporary cloud credentials. What core design flaw enabled this extraction?
opts: The database engine automatically processed unescaped parameters
The metadata endpoint implicitly trusted requests from the host
The browser automatically forwarded ambient identity credentials
The application failed to enforce strong administrative passwords

wrongFeedback.2: Browser-managed ambient credentials enable client-side CSRF, whereas here the request originated directly from the backend cloud server.

q: A web server processes outgoing webhook notifications configured by end users. What network-level architecture control prevents attackers from abusing this service to scan private internal corporate subnets?
opts: Blocking incoming ICMP echo requests at the edge perimeter
Terminating secure socket layer sessions at an edge load balancer
Restricting server egress traffic from reaching RFC 1918 spaces
Implementing web application firewall inspection on client inputs
exp: Egress filtering at the network firewall prevents the application server from initiating connections to private internal address ranges (RFC 1918), neutralizing internal SSRF pivots.

wrongFeedback.0: Disabling incoming ICMP stops external ping sweeps, but does not block the backend server from initiating internal TCP scans.
wrongFeedback.1: SSL termination offloads encryption processing at the perimeter, providing no restrictions on where backend servers route outbound requests.
wrongFeedback.3: While a WAF provides Layer 7 perimeter filtering, it is an application-layer control; egress firewall rules provide the definitive network-level control.

q: A document converter accepts external URLs to import text files. An attacker enters file:///etc/passwd, and the server returns the contents of the local user configuration file. What design oversight permitted this bypass?
opts: Failing to restrict supported protocol handlers within the URL parser
Allowing dynamic database rollbacks during unhandled file read errors
Omitting SameSite attributes on sensitive administrative cookies
Storing operating system configuration files in encrypted disk blocks
exp: URL parsers should explicitly permit only web protocols (such as HTTP and HTTPS); allowing alternative URI schemes like file:// or gopher:// enables direct local file disclosure.

wrongFeedback.2: The SameSite cookie attribute mitigates client-side CSRF, whereas this attack targets local server files via backend URI handlers.
wrongFeedback.3: Full-disk encryption protects data at rest against physical theft, but does not prevent the running operating system from reading files requested by a valid service.

q: A developer blocks requests to 127.0.0.1 and localhost to protect an internal API. An attacker enters http://2130706433 (the integer format of 127.0.0.1) and successfully reaches the API. Why did this defense fail?
opts: Integer IP representations force web proxies to drop request headers
String-based blacklists fail to account for alternative address formats
Transport layer encryption automatically decodes non-standard IP strings
The API gateway bypassed routing checks due to session state caching
exp: Input validation based on blacklisting specific string patterns (like literal 127.0.0.1) fails against obfuscated representations such as integer notation, hex, octal, or custom DNS lookups that resolve to loopback.

wrongFeedback.0: Proxies do not strip request headers simply because an IP address is formatted as a 32-bit integer.
wrongFeedback.2: Transport encryption (TLS) protects payload confidentiality; it does not parse or rewrite destination IP address encodings.
wrongFeedback.3: Session caching maintains active user state and does not alter how host addresses are parsed or resolved.

q: A web server contains an unpatched SSRF vulnerability. However, when an attacker sends a GET request to the cloud metadata address (http://169.254.169.254), the request returns 401 Unauthorized and denies credential extraction. Which mitigation successfully stopped this exploit?
opts: Requiring custom session token headers for all metadata requests
Disabling all inbound security group rules on web application ports
Rotating cloud infrastructure access keys automatically every 24 hours
Enforcing context-aware output encoding across incoming HTTP queries
exp: Modern cloud metadata protections (such as AWS IMDSv2) require a session-oriented PUT request to obtain an authorization token header before querying metadata, blocking simple GET-based SSRF exploits.
